bull_bear.body:
- 5-yr term debt; 1-yr moratorium; repayment from Q3FY27 over ~4 yrs (early repayment optional).
- FY26 CFO/FCF negative due to timing (Brazil anticipation, war receivable delays, deposit reclassification); target reversion to >100% EBITDA-to-cash conversion by end FY27.
- No buyback/dividend commentary on call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- Geopolitics/war: Middle East + Israel demand still below pre-war; recovery non-linear; further escalation a downside.
- Airline capacity cuts / fare volatility; corridor disruption.
- Working-capital/cash-flow drag if timing items don't reverse as expected.
- Global peers resetting take-rates lower → competitive pressure (mgmt comfortable).
- LATAM/Brazil structural FX + tax (IOF) headwinds.
- Classic integration execution (platform migration mid-way).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic / confident. Candid about March washout and cash-flow drag; emphasized resilience of luxury/premium demand and that war is short-term. Declined to quantify Q1 growth (status-quo caveat repeated). Open to suggestions (constant-currency reporting).
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- War actually masked stronger underlying growth — "if the war had not happened, numbers would have been much stronger"; March's lost GTV (esp. hotel) would have largely flowed to bottom line (Q4 EBITDA ~Rs. 110 cr; analyst implied Rs. 30–50 cr lost in March).
- Higher airfares are GTV-neutral-to-positive: fewer tickets for same GTV.
- B2B travel growing faster than B2C (online B2C saturating).
- Expedia's 20% B2B growth not viewed as direct competition (Expedia is also a TBO supplier).
- Classic carries negative working capital, but acquisition accounting subsumes opening benefit into investing CF — cash benefit only accrues as WC goes more negative going forward.
- AI: mgmt sees only internal productivity gains so far, no business-model disruption (MCPs/ChatGPT integrations not yet driving real business).
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

business.body:
- **Hotels & ancillary:** higher-margin; strong growth; expected to grow faster than air → mix tailwind to margins.
- **Air:** GTV ~Rs. 3,400 cr organic. Q1FY27 trajectory "a shade better than Q4." Airline capacity cuts (domestic + international) seen as temporary; higher fares mean fewer tickets needed for same GTV; corridor shifts (away from Middle East; toward intra-Europe, Asia-Pacific, Japan for HNIs, Europe for ultra-HNIs).
- **Geographies:** Middle East (largest source market) + Israel severely hit by war, still below pre-war but recovering; demand diverted to Europe/Southern Europe (platform agnostic). NA strong (seasonal Jan–Mar). LATAM/Brazil moderate growth (Brazil anticipation discontinued Q3, IOF tax + currency headwinds).
- **Mix:** Hotel retail vs API ~50:50 on GTV; retail higher share of GP.
business.title: Segment (hotels / air / geographies)

business.body:
- "Top Global 2-sided B2B Travel Distribution Platform" and "Among Top 4 B2B Travel distribution platforms globally"; the platform "Connects travel buyers across the world serving end travelers with globally distributed travel suppliers to seamlessly create joyful experiences for all travelers."
- The industry-landscape slide maps distribution across an economy-to-luxury and low-to-high complexity grid, splitting Enterprise Buyers (API Distribution, "Traditionally served by Bed Banks") from Retail Buyers (Platform led Distribution, "Traditionally served by Regional Aggregators") — positioning TBO across both.
- Platform value proposition framed as five needs: Discovery, Trust ("Supplier onboarding is curated by TBO with strict SLAs"), Payments ("Guarantee payment to Supplier", "Transact in respective local currencies"), Service ("24x7, multi-lingual pre- and post-booking support") and matching buyers to preferences; "Our platform is core to retail buyers and suppliers."
- Demand thesis: an ageing, more prosperous world (rising lifespans, incomes and falling fertility and work hours) makes outbound travel a "New Megatrend", with assisted travel "a very large opportunity", longer trips with multiple services stitched together, and older affluent travellers wanting "expertise, comfort, convenience, and novelty".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Reporting basis] The deck reports two bases side by side — "Reported (TBO Organic + CV)" and "TBO Organic" — for transacting buyers, GTV, revenue, gross profit and Adj. EBITDA, so group and organic figures must not be conflated.
- [M&A] Journey slide records inorganic growth: "First Acquisition – Island Hopper" (2018), "Acquired Bookabed AG" (2022), plus "Acquired Jumbonline S.L.U." and "Acquired Classic Vacations", with the latter two's year labels not cleanly bound in the extract.
- [Ownership history] Naspers acquired a stake in TBO, later "Affirma acquired Naspers' Stake in TBO", and "General Atlantic acquired stake in TBO"; TBO "goes Public and lists on NSE and BSE" in 2024.
- [Milestones] Incorporated 2006; commenced international operations in UAE (2011); commenced operations in Brazil; "$1Bn GTV Milestone"; "$10Mn GTV in one day Milestone".
- [Quarter framing] The Q4'FY26 summary slide is titled "Strong quarter, demonstrating structural resilience against geopolitical headwinds".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- EBITDA/GTV ~1%, stable 3 yrs; expected to expand from FY27.
- SG&A grew ~16% in FY26 (front-loaded H1; tapered by Q4). Going forward SG&A growth to slow but not flatten — sales-force expansion is the growth engine.
- Operating leverage materializes only when enterprise GTV growth surpasses SG&A growth; ex-Middle East margins already improving.
- Classic SG&A ~Rs. 110 cr over last two quarters; cost-reduction not committed (uplift/efficiency story pending platform migration).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4FY26 (this call):** Q4 & FY26 results. War (started ~end-Feb 2026) caused March washout; Middle East + Israel hit. Still grew YoY top & bottom line. Q4 EBITDA ~Rs. 110 cr; EBITDA/GTV ~1%; air GTV ~Rs. 3,400 cr; FX tailwind ~4–5% on FY hotel GTV. Classic ~6 months in, integration ~halfway (complete by end CY26). FY26 GTV growth ~22% (15% new agents / 7–8% old). SG&A ~16%, to taper. CFO/FCF negative (timing) → target >100% conversion end-FY27. ETR ~18–18.5%. 5-yr debt, repay from Q3FY27. Voya AI luxury tool launched. NA transacting agents 4,800→6,000 QoQ. Guidance: Q1FY27 > Q4 and > Q1FY26 (YoY+QoQ), long-term ~20%+ aspiration.
latest_quarter.title: QoQ Log

outlook.body:
- **GTV growth:** No hard number given. Q1FY27 expected better than Q4 AND better than Q1FY26 (both YoY and QoQ) at status-quo geopolitics. Long-term aspiration: grow "north of 20%" / early-to-mid 20s.
- **Take-rate:** Maintain at current levels — no improvement targeted, no downward pressure expected short-to-midterm (despite global peers cutting take-rates). EBITDA/GTV ratio expected to move up from FY27 as SG&A tapers + hotels mix rises.
- **Supplier/buyer adds:** Monthly transacting buyers grew "very dramatically" YoY; NA transacting agents grew 4,800 → 6,000 QoQ (partly Jan–Mar seasonality). FY26 GTV growth ~22%, of which ~15% from new (FY26-added) agents and ~7–8% from pre-FY26 cohorts (depressed by Middle East). Agent cohort roughly doubles its business in the subsequent year.
- **Margin:** SG&A growth to taper (won't go flat); top-line to grow faster than SG&A → operating-leverage / margin expansion from FY27. CFO/FCF target back to >100% conversion by end of FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance — CRITICAL

outlook.body:
- North America build-out via Classic + TBO NA (one combined business); platform/supply/demand integration to complete by end of CY26/Q3.
- APAC: Australia investments delivering; large API partners based in APAC selling globally; small base but optimistic (price-competitive vs EU/NA).
- Europe: growth from KAM/unit-economics-driven penetration; KAM maturity curve ~6–9 months to meaningful productivity/break-even.
- Voya AI tool launched for ultra-luxury supply + AI-led complex-itinerary workflow for travel advisors.
outlook.title: Pipeline (new markets / suppliers)

outlook.body:
- Classic Vacations integration unlocks NA luxury; TBO supply being selectively opened (curated luxury hotels only) into Classic ecosystem — already a "fair/meaningful share" of Classic's business; connectivity established.
- Voya = AI-first luxury adjacency; bet that complex luxury itineraries stay agent-mediated even as AI grows.
- Luxury anchoring thesis: premium/luxury demand more resilient to war/inflation/geopolitics.
- Middle East tourism boards planning aggressive re-investment in recovery — potential sharp rebound (UAE post-pandemic playbook cited).
outlook.title: Growth / optionality (M&A, new regions, ancillary)

deepdive.thesis: TBO is a global B2B travel-distribution platform monetizing GTV via take-rate, with structural growth from (a) market-development investment (sales/KAM expansion → onboarding new travel agents and driving them through T1/T5/T10 transaction journey), (b) shift toward higher-take-rate markets (North America, Europe) and higher-margin hotels mix vs air, and (c) the luxury/curated adjacency (Classic Vacations + Voya AI tool). Q4FY26 demonstrated resilience: despite the war (started end-Feb) severely hitting its largest source market (Middle East) and Israel (a Top-7 source country), the company still grew YoY on both top and bottom line. Jan/Feb showed strong operating leverage and margin expansion; March was "a complete washout." Mgmt expects Q1FY27 better than both Q4 and the year-ago quarter, with green shoots of operating leverage as SG&A growth tapers below GTV growth.

Run the AI Centre of Excellence as a multi-year agenda and continue building internal platforms (Epicenter, Voya) as long-term AI orchestration layers, extending AI from assistive tooling toward autonomous, agent-led workflow execution across the travel transaction lifecycle.

Continue expanding reach by strengthening local execution, adding feet-on-street, sales and account-management teams and servicing depth across priority geographies, accepting upfront cost ahead of cohort maturity.

Continue evaluating and pursuing disciplined, value-accretive acquisitions that strengthen network effects, deepen capabilities, expand geographic relevance or accelerate participation in strategic segments, including larger, strategically aligned opportunities.

Improve operating leverage: FY 2026 included investments necessary for future growth, and the next phase will focus on scaling activity through a more productive commercial engine and leaner AI-enabled workflows.
Scale North America beyond Classic Vacations through integration, advisor engagement, supply expansion and long-term value creation in the US market.

Deepen platform activity - agent activation, repeat usage, cohort productivity and share-of-wallet expansion - to convert the agent base added during FY 2026 into a larger and more productive platform base.
Management explicitly flags that corridor risk remains real and that diversification reduces exposure but does not eliminate volatility.

Continue broadening the geographic mix, deepening supply across alternate destinations and improving the platform's ability to respond to changing travel patterns in real time, because corridor risk remains real and regional concentration can be reduced but not eliminated.
Improve operating leverage: after an FY 2026 investment year, the next phase is to scale activity through a more productive commercial engine and leaner AI-enabled workflows.

Continue evaluating acquisitions that strengthen network effects, deepen capabilities, expand geographic relevance or accelerate participation in strategic segments; management states it continues to look for larger, strategically aligned opportunities.

Continue expanding direct supply, premium inventory and ancillary product lines to increase platform relevance and share of wallet, building both the workflow layer (Voya) and the supply layer (Platinum, direct contracting) needed for premium, multi-component journeys.
Continue investing in luxury, assisted travel, Platinum, Voya and high-value travel use cases.
Continue building AI-native workflows by redesigning operations, servicing, supplier management, software development, commercial productivity and connected journeys.
Scale North America beyond the Classic Vacations starting point through integration, advisor engagement, supply expansion and long-term value creation in the US market.

Deepen platform activity by converting the agent base added during FY 2026 into a larger and more productive platform base, focusing on agent activation, repeat usage, cohort productivity and share-of-wallet expansion.
Continue to invest in and build infrastructure, technology, network and service capabilities to create sustainable moats.

risks.note: Conflicts, travel advisories, airspace restrictions, sanctions and aviation incidents may disrupt important travel corridors and affect demand patterns. This is not theoretical for TBO: FY 2026 saw an India-Pakistan flare-up, the broader Iran-US-Israel conflict, aviation disruptions, a major air tragedy and weather events, and March 2026 - a seasonally important period - affected both source and destination markets across approximately 40% of relevant travel corridors, producing weaker demand, cancellations and volatility in booking patterns. Airspace restrictions and instability in the Middle East are stated to have caused a 70% drop in demand in early 2026. Management's mitigation is geographic diversification across source markets, broader supply coverage, active corridor monitoring and reallocation toward alternate demand flows, and it explicitly concedes that diversification reduces exposure but does not eliminate volatility and that corridor risk remains real. Geopolitical Conflicts was newly ADDED as a BRSR material topic in FY 2025-26.
risks.risk: Geopolitical and regional disruption of travel corridors

risks.note: As a global B2B platform managing high-volume transactional, payment and customer data streams across multiple jurisdictions, the Company faces material operational and compliance exposure from systemic IT vulnerabilities; prolonged network outages, infrastructure failures or sophisticated cyber incidents can immediately disrupt downstream booking fulfilment, cause revenue leakage and severely compromise partner trust. Privacy and Data Security is the FIRST-listed BRSR material issue, rated both risk and opportunity, with the stated negative implication being exposure to legal penalties and significant breach-recovery costs. Mitigation is stated as enterprise-grade threat detection, data encryption, regular assessments, access controls, platform resilience, monitoring and audit, and strict compliance with applicable data-privacy regulations. The Corporate Governance Report separately makes cybersecurity and data protection a standing board-level oversight area.

AI-enabled interfaces and agentic commerce models may increasingly influence how travel is discovered, planned, booked and fulfilled, creating intermediary bypass risk in simpler use cases. This is the risk most specific to the business model and management engages it directly rather than deflecting: its stated counter-thesis is that complex, premium and multi-component travel will continue to require expertise, robust fulfilment infrastructure, curated supply, servicing capability, payment infrastructure and operational reliability, and that AI bots will become demand channels FEEDING travel distribution platforms rather than replacing them. Mitigation is continued investment in AI-enabled workflows, infrastructure relevance, fulfilment capability and advisor-led complex travel. Note the two-sided nature: management also frames AI as a moat risk in the other direction, observing that frontier models can recreate an entire platform front-end at a fraction of cost and time, which is why it argues differentiation must sit in infrastructure, integrations, relationships and data systems rather than interface.
risks.risk: AI-driven disintermediation of the distribution channel

risks.note: The business model depends on relationships with airlines, hotel chains, aggregators and ancillary providers, and changes in supplier economics, commission structures, pricing models or direct distribution strategies may affect profitability and competitiveness. The structural exposure is that suppliers can choose to go direct and bypass the distribution layer. Mitigation is expansion of direct contracting (direct supply share rose to 35% in FY 2026 from 33.9% in FY 2025), diversified supplier relationships and long-term partnership management.

The market remains highly competitive with global online travel companies, regional platforms, supplier-direct channels and specialist vertical players participating; competitive intensity may increase pressure on pricing, commissions, customer acquisition costs and margins. Mitigation is stated as continued investment in technology, servicing capability, supply breadth, premium travel positioning and differentiated partner workflows.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity in global travel distribution

risks.note: Inflation, interest rates, currency movements and slower discretionary spending may affect booking volumes, travel frequency, destination choices and traveller spend; currency weakness in outbound source markets may specifically affect affordability and mix. Travel is discretionary, so this risk is amplified relative to staples-like businesses. Mitigation is diversified market exposure, product mix toward higher-value categories, active commercial management and customer-cohort diversification.

Not presented in the AR's risk table but flagged repeatedly by management as a live watch-item: hiring sales teams and adding feet-on-street carries upfront cost, newly onboarded agents take time to activate, mature and scale, and the full operating leverage from the FY 2026 investment cycle will emerge only over time as cohorts become more productive and the cost base stabilises. Management states these investments elevated SG&A growth in the first half of FY 2026 before moderating from Q3 FY 2026, and concedes that 'sales investments can create future growth, but they also carry upfront costs before operating leverage is fully visible' and that 'AI improves productivity, but it does not transform operating models overnight'.
risks.risk: Execution and cost-timing risk in the commercial investment cycle

risks.note: The North America strategy rests on a single acquisition. Management describes the integration - spanning platform, supply, commercial and talent - as an execution priority with expected completion by Q3 of the current fiscal (stated as FY 2027 in the Letter to Shareholders) and explicitly characterises it as 'a multi-year value creation journey' that is 'not complete'. The stated intent is not simply to consolidate Classic Vacations but to combine its advisor relationships, luxury supply and servicing expertise with TBO's technology, global supply network, commercial reach and operating discipline - a two-way integration that is correspondingly harder to execute.
risks.risk: Integration risk on the Classic Vacations acquisition and dependence on M&A for the North America build

meta.thesis: TBO is a global B2B travel-distribution platform monetizing GTV via take-rate, with structural growth from (a) market-development investment (sales/KAM expansion → onboarding new travel agents and driving them through T1/T5/T10 transaction journey), (b) shift toward higher-take-rate markets (North America, Europe) and higher-margin hotels mix vs air, and (c) the luxury/curated adjacency (Classic Vacations + Voya AI tool). Q4FY26 demonstrated resilience: despite the war (started end-Feb) severely hitting its largest source market (Middle East) and Israel (a Top-7 source country), the company still grew YoY on both top and bottom line. Jan/Feb showed strong operating leverage and margin expansion; March was "a complete washout." Mgmt expects Q1FY27 better than both Q4 and the year-ago quarter, with green shoots of operating leverage as SG&A growth tapers below GTV growth.
